meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first.
Don't thank me. Who entered that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
You're leading me, Hale, and I've cross-examined better witnesses than you for twenty years. I asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
That's two, and what my son does after school is not your business. Is there anything on Owen's record right now, yes or no?
So it's at least possible he used it once?

I'm not answering a hypothetical about my son, and he wrote that essay. Three leading questions and not one document. Show me something with a date on it, Hale, or I'm walking upstairs to the principal.
I agreed to nothing, and I'm writing down that you tried that. Owen's essay is his. Document, or the principal.
